metaData.originalTitle: Qwen-AgentWorld 开源：让 Agent 学会“先预测，再行动”
metaData.title: Qwen-AgentWorld Open-Source: Teaching Agents to 'Predict First, Act Later'
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Tongyi Lab open-sources Qwen-AgentWorld, the first native language world model that starts environment modeling from the continued pre-training stage, surpassing state-of-the-art models like GPT-5.4 on AgentWorldBench, and demonstrating two application paradigms: controllable simulation and cross-task generalization.
metaData.summary: The article introduces Tongyi Lab's open-source Qwen-AgentWorld, the first language world model covering seven domains. Through a three-stage training pipeline—CPT (Continued Pre-Training) → SFT (Supervised Fine-Tuning) → RL (Reinforcement Learning)—it surpasses models like GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.8 on AgentWorldBench. The article details key design choices in the training process (round-level informational entropy loss masking, chain-of-thought rejection sampling, hybrid reward signals) and introduces the AgentWorldBench evaluation benchmark. On the application side, two paradigms are explored: as a decoupled environment simulator, controllable Sim RL outperforms real-environment training on MCP and search tasks and generalizes to unseen environments; as a unified agent foundation model, LWM warm-up training yields significant gains in untouched domains, indicating that next-state prediction is a transferable meta-reasoning ability. The project is open-sourced.

mainPoints.point: The three-stage world model training pipeline (CPT → SFT → RL) systematically enhances environment modeling ability.
mainPoints.explanation: CPT injects environment knowledge, SFT activates chain-of-thought reasoning, and RL refines simulation authenticity. The overall approach outperforms GPT-5.4 on AgentWorldBench, achieving an 8.66-point improvement even at small model scale, validating the pipeline's effectiveness.

mainPoints.point: Controllable simulation enables Sim RL to surpass real-environment training on multiple tasks.
mainPoints.explanation: By using natural language instructions to control simulator behavior (e.g., injecting API errors, paginated responses, etc.), performance improves by 12.3 on MCPMark and 16.3 on WideSearch. On WideSearch, it even surpasses Real RL trained with real search engines (F1 50.3% vs 45.6%).

mainPoints.point: Next-state prediction serves as a transferable meta-reasoning ability, enabling cross-task generalization.
mainPoints.explanation: After single-round, non-tool-call LWM RL warm-up training, direct transfer to multi-round tool-call benchmarks yields improvements of 11.3, 9.7, and 9.0 respectively on three completely unseen domains (Claw-Eval, QwenClawBench, etc.), without any additional fine-tuning.

keyQuotes: Rather than trial and error in real environments, it's better to first teach AI to 'predict what the environment will do'.
CPT injects, SFT activates, RL refines.
Controllable simulation shapes agent behavior in ways that real environments cannot achieve.
Next-state prediction teaches the agent to simulate environmental responses before acting.

relatedArticles.title: From Transparent Development to Systems Engineering: AgentScope 2.0 Released
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: AgentScope 2.0 upgrades from transparent development to systems engineering, focusing on stable operation, security control, and production-level deployment capabilities for agents in real-world scenarios.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: 215 SOTA Benchmarks + Emergent Vibe Coding! Qwen3.5-Omni Released
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Tongyi Lab releases Qwen3.5-Omni, a native omni-modal large model that achieves SOTA in 215 benchmarks, supporting real-time audio-visual interaction, voice cloning, and emergent Vibe Coding capabilities.

relatedArticles.title: Qwen3.6-Plus: A Major Leap in Coding Agent Capabilities!
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Qwen-Lab releases Qwen3.6-Plus, focusing on strengthening the stable execution of Coding Agents, with support for a 1M context window and deep multimodal reasoning.

relatedArticles.title: Redefining Skill Development: A Step-by-Step Guide & One-Stop Development Assistant Launch
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces the concept of AI Agent Skill, including its directory structure, writing standards, release process, and cross-platform challenges. It also launches a one-stop Skill development assistant, skill-dev-aio, designed to free developers from tedious tool learning and allow them to focus on experience and judgment.

relatedArticles.title: Qwen3.7-Max Redefines the Foundation of AI Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Alibaba Tongyi Lab releases Qwen3.7-Max, demonstrating long-horizon agent stability in extreme stress tests with 35 hours of continuous autonomous execution and 1,158 tool calls without interruption, achieving cross-framework generalization through a decoupled training architecture.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: All-in-One Text, Image, and Video! An Open-Source Framework for Multimodal Knowledge Bases
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Tongyi Lab has open-sourced the VimRAG framework, which leverages Dynamic Acyclic Graphs (DAG) and Graph-Guided Policy Optimization to solve cross-modal retrieval and long-context reasoning challenges in mixed-media knowledge bases.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Harness Engineering: Finding the Shell That Keeps AI from Going Rogue—Insights from 14 Engineering Articles | Hao's Trend Talk
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of "Harness Engineering," a core technology in the AI Agent field. It reveals how to compensate for model shortcomings through a three-layer management architecture and proposes the logic of "Compensation Surface Migration" that evolves with model capabilities.
